newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to study underground metro in Alexandria.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to study underground metro in Alexandria.

text.p: Egypt has contracted a French-Egyptian consortium to study the feasibility of setting up an underground metro in the Mediterranean city of Alexandria, a senior official said on Thursday.

"The study is a preparation for an invitation to international bidders to execute the first phase of the project," chairman of the National Authority of Tunnels, El-Husseini Abdel Salam, told Reuters.
The $5.6 million-contract was awarded to the consortium which includes three French firms, an Italian firm and the Egyptian firm Arab Consulting Engineers, Abdel Salam added.
The line, which will be built in three stages, will be extended for 55 km (34 miles) from the east to the west of the city. The length of the first stage will be 22 km.
Egypt has built a 50-km (30 mile) long underground line in Cairo and has completed the first phase of its second line. It plans to have three lines in the city.
